Rules that generalize quasi-identifier values

Source: R/anon_generalize.R
generalize_rules.Rd

Each function returns a rule for anon_generalize(): anon_band() puts numbers into bands, anon_round() rounds them, and anon_fold() merges small categories into one. A rule is also a function: call it on a vector to apply it, as in anon_band(5)(ages). Rules keep the vector's type, class and attributes, so code written for the original values still runs.

Usage

anon_band(width, top = NULL, bottom = NULL, value = c("lower", "midpoint"))

anon_round(digits)

anon_fold(min_n, to)

Arguments

width

Width of each band, a positive number (for example 5 for 5-year age bands). Bands start at bottom when given, otherwise at 0: with width = 5 they are 0-4.99..., 5-9.99..., and so on, whatever the data's range; with bottom = 18 they are 18-22.99..., 23-27.99...

top, bottom

Optional limits: values at or above top become top, and values at or below bottom become bottom, instead of being banded (top and bottom coding). HIPAA Safe Harbor, for example, groups ages over 89 into one category, which top = 90 gives.

value

The number that stands for a band: "lower" (default), its lower bound, or "midpoint", its middle, kept within bottom and top. Either is a representative, not a subject's real value.

digits

Number of decimal places to round to, as in round(); negative values round to tens (-1), hundreds (-2) and so on.

min_n

Smallest number of subjects a category must hold to be kept. Categories held by fewer subjects become to. Subjects are counted, not rows (see Details).

to

The value small categories become, such as "OTHER". There is no default: choose a value that is allowed in the column (for SDTM, a term in the variable's controlled terminology). A number for a numeric column.

Value

An object of class "anon_generalize_rule", a function function(x, subjects = NULL) that returns x generalized. subjects (used by anon_fold() only) gives the subject of each element of x.

Details

Bands and rounding apply to numeric vectors (double or integer, also haven-labelled). The result stays numeric; an integer vector stays integer, and a rule that would give it a number that isn't whole (a midpoint of an odd width, say) is an error, as is one too large for an integer. Missing values, haven user-defined missing values, and values that carry a haven value label (codes such as 99 for "not done") are left as they are. Rounding follows round().

Folding applies to character, factor and numeric vectors (also haven-labelled). Missing and blank values are never folded or counted, and to itself is never folded (it can stay small: measure again with anon_risk() and suppress what remains with anon_suppress()). A factor keeps its class: the folded levels are removed (with unused levels held by fewer than min_n subjects) and to is added as the last level if it isn't one already. Called on a vector, each element counts as one subject unless subjects gives the subject of each element. In anon_generalize(), subjects are counted by the key, across every dataset where the same column has the same rule.

haven value labels are kept where they still describe the values: a fold drops the labels of folded categories, and a band or rounding drops the label of any code that values moved into or out of.

See also

anon_generalize() to apply rules to datasets, anon_rule() for test results such as weight in vs.

Examples

ages <- c(23, 37, 41, 58, 64, 91)
anon_band(10, top = 90)(ages)
#> [1] 20 30 40 50 60 90
anon_band(10, value = "midpoint")(ages)
#> [1] 25 35 45 55 65 95
anon_round(-1)(c(153.2, 171.8))
#> [1] 150 170

race <- c("WHITE", "WHITE", "ASIAN", "BLACK OR AFRICAN AMERICAN", "WHITE")
anon_fold(2, to = "OTHER")(race)
#> [1] "WHITE" "WHITE" "OTHER" "OTHER" "WHITE"
anon_fold(2, to = "OTHER")
#> <anon rule> anon_fold(min_n = 2, to = "OTHER")
